Tessa — thanks for taking the time today. Helpful call; wanted to capture two quick follow-ups so my team can continue the internal review:

1) Subprocessors list: can you share the list of third-party telemetry and analytics vendors that may receive telemetry or metrics derived from API requests? We need vendor names, purpose, and whether any raw request data is forwarded.
2) Logging & retention: what logs are kept (request/response, access logs, raw tokens) and default retention windows? Will you provide a log retention SLA for enterprise customers?
3) Data residency: we run in a US region but need confirmation that model inference and logs can be kept within AWS us-west-2. Any cross-region telemetry exports?

Sarah — appreciated the conversation. Recap and concrete next steps below. I pulled out the items you listed and added owners/timeline on our side so your security team has a single reference.

Summary answers (high level):
- Subprocessors: we maintain an exportable inventory. Primary telemetry vendors: TelemetryCo (metrics/usage only), MetricsHub (pipeline health), and S3 (storage for batch logs). No raw customer request bodies are forwarded to telemetry vendors by default; telemetry is event-level metrics and hashed identifiers. Full vendor list attached (redwood-subprocessors-inventory.csv).
- Logging & retention: by default, access and inference logs are retained 30 days for hosted customers; enterprise plans can request extended retention up to 365 days under contract. We can offer 90-day retention as a standard on Dedicated agreements (see attached redwood-telemetry-sla.xlsx).
- Data residency: inference and primary logs can be pinned to a region (us-west-2). Telemetry export jobs run in the pinned region unless a marketplace integration is explicitly enabled.
- PII handling: we have automated scrubbers for known PII patterns (SSNs, credit card numbers, emails) before telemetry extraction. Any customer-provided allowlist/denylist is supported; we can also run a hashing-only flow where identifiers are hashed with a customer-managed salt.

Action items and owners:
- Tessa: share inventory CSV and SLA spreadsheet (attached) — today.
- Vivek: confirm technical notes about hashing, KV-cache behavior, and whether caller-supplied keys are included in logs — by EOD Fri.
- Monica: schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your security lead to walk the questionnaire and any sample logs — propose Mon / Tue next week.

If that timeline works for you we'll try to hit your review window next Thursday. Happy to jump on another call if you want a short demo of how telemetry is sampled.

Thanks,

Subject: TECH NOTES — telemetry & PII handling (short)

- TelemetryCo: processes aggregated usage metrics only. We send event-level metrics (timestamp, endpoint, status_code, token_count, hashed_user_id). No raw request/response payloads are transmitted by default.
- Hashing: we support HMAC-SHA256 hashing of identifiers with a customer-provided salt (preferred). If customers request, we can run deterministic hashing for correlation across datasets.
- KV cache: cache keys are ephemeral and not exported; cache misses/hits are logged as counts only.
- Logs: access logs include request timestamp, model variant, latencies, and token counts. Response text is not stored in access logs unless the customer enables debug logging — debug logging is off by default and requires a contract clause.
- Retention: default 30 days; enterprise options: 90, 180, 365 days. We can provide export hooks (S3) for customers that want to ship logs to their own bucket daily.

Mark any questions you'd like me to expand in the questionnaire; I can pull sample redacted logs for Sarah's team if they want to see the shape.

Vivek
